---
title: Idempotency
description: Ensuring consistent step recordings in Threadify
---

**Idempotency** ensures that recording the same step multiple times has the same effect as recording it once. This prevents duplicate operations and ensures consistent execution when retries or network issues occur.

### Idempotency Keys

#### Auto-generated Keys
- Threadify automatically generates unique keys for each step

#### Custom Keys
- You can provide your own idempotency keys for business-level deduplication
- Example: Use order ID for payment step

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Node.js">
```javascript
import { Threadify } from '@threadify/sdk';

const connection = await Threadify.connect('api-key', 'payment-service');
const thread = await connection.start('order_fulfillment', 'merchant');

// Auto-generated idempotency key (default)
const paymentStep = thread.step('payment_processed');
// Threadify generates unique key automatically

// Custom idempotency key for business-level deduplication
const orderPaymentStep = thread.step('payment_processed')
  .idempotencyKey(`order_${orderId}_payment`);
// Ensures one payment per order regardless of retries
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### When Idempotency Matters

#### Network Retries
<Tabs>
<Tab title="Node.js">
```javascript
import { Threadify } from '@threadify/sdk';

// Client retries due to network timeout - Threadify handles deduplication
const connection = await Threadify.connect('api-key', 'payment-service');
const thread = await connection.start('order_fulfillment', 'merchant');

await processPaymentWithRetry('order_123'); // First attempt - success
await processPaymentWithRetry('order_123'); // Retry - ignored as duplicate

async function processPaymentWithRetry(orderId) {
  const paymentStep = thread.step('payment_processed')
    .idempotencyKey(`payment_${orderId}`);
  
  try {
    const payment = await paymentGateway.charge(orderId);
    await paymentStep.success({ transactionId: payment.id });
    return payment;
  } catch (error) {
    await paymentStep.failed({ message: error.message });
    throw error;
  }
}
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Service Restarts
<Tabs>
<Tab title="Node.js">
```javascript
// Service crashes after processing but before acknowledging
const paymentStep = thread.step('payment_processed')
  .idempotencyKey(`payment_${orderId}`);

try {
  const payment = await paymentGateway.charge(orderId);
  await paymentStep.success({ transactionId: payment.id });
  // Service crashes here
} catch (error) {
  await paymentStep.failed({ message: error.message });
}

// Service restarts - same idempotency key prevents duplicate
const restartedPaymentStep = thread.step('payment_processed')
  .idempotencyKey(`payment_${orderId}`); // Same key!
// Threadify recognizes this as duplicate and returns existing result
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Race Conditions
<Tabs>
<Tab title="Node.js">
```javascript
// Multiple services process same event simultaneously
const orderId = 'order_123';

// Service A processes order
const serviceA = await Threadify.connect('api-key', 'service-a');
const threadA = await serviceA.getThread('thread-uuid');
const stepA = threadA.step('order_processed')
  .idempotencyKey(`order_${orderId}`);

// Service B tries to process same order (race condition)
const serviceB = await Threadify.connect('api-key', 'service-b');
const threadB = await serviceB.getThread('thread-uuid');
const stepB = threadB.step('order_processed')
  .idempotencyKey(`order_${orderId}`); // Same key!

// Only one succeeds - Threadify prevents duplicate processing
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Idempotency in Action

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Node.js">
```javascript
import { Threadify } from '@threadify/sdk';

class PaymentService {
  constructor() {
    this.connection = null;
  }

  async initialize() {
    this.connection = await Threadify.connect('api-key', 'payment-service');
  }

  async processPayment(orderId, amount) {
    const thread = await this.connection.start('order_fulfillment', 'merchant');
    
    // Use order ID as idempotency key - prevents duplicate charges
    const paymentStep = thread.step('payment_processed')
      .idempotencyKey(`payment_${orderId}`);
    
    try {
      const payment = await paymentGateway.charge({
        orderId,
        amount,
        currency: 'USD'
      });
      
      await paymentStep
        .addContext({ 
          transactionId: payment.id,
          amount: payment.amount,
          currency: payment.currency,
          paymentMethod: payment.method
        })
        .success();
        
      console.log(`Payment processed: ${payment.id}`);
      return payment;
      
    } catch (error) {
      await paymentStep.failed({ 
        message: error.message,
        errorCode: error.code,
        retryable: error.retryable || false
      });
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

// Usage - can be called multiple times safely
const paymentService = new PaymentService();
await paymentService.initialize();

await paymentService.processPayment('order_123', 99.99); // Success
await paymentService.processPayment('order_123', 99.99); // Ignored as duplicate
await paymentService.processPayment('order_123', 99.99); // Ignored as duplicate
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Best Practices

- **Business keys** - Use business identifiers when possible
- **Consistent naming** - Follow patterns for key generation
- **Scope appropriately** - Keys should be unique within scope
- **Don't reuse** - Never reuse idempotency keys for different operations

### Benefits

- **Retry safety** - Services can retry without side effects
- **Consistency** - Thread state remains consistent
- **Recovery** - Systems can recover from failures safely
- **Exactly-once processing** - Prevents duplicate operations
